title: A Letter for the Confession
premise: When the coffin of Harborline's founder, Edmund Voss, is exhumed for a centennial ceremony and found empty, concierge Casper Thackeray is drawn in because the exhumation order was signed with a letter they once delivered — a confession never sent. Casper discovers that three 'accidental' deaths over thirty years were all witnesses to the night Voss vanished, and that the town's founding families built their fortunes on a smuggling run gone wrong. As the tide recedes to reveal Voss's remains beneath the old pier, Casper must choose between exposing the killer — the dying matriarch who has been their quiet benefactor — or letting the town keep its beloved lie. In the end, Casper delivers the confession at last, trading the truth's release for the killer's peaceful surrender, and finds belonging not in Harborline's approval but in being finally seen.
about_author: Lena Crane spent a decade working night desks at coastal hotels, where she learned that guests tell front desks what they tell no one else. She writes mysteries about people who watch quietly and are watched too late.

chapters.title: The Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: Casper Thackeray, POV. During Harborline's centennial preparations, the founder's coffin is opened and found empty; among the crowd, Casper recognizes the exhumation order as the letter they privately delivered years ago. The chapter establishes Casper's gift for noticing and their outsider status. Emotional beat: unease — the past has knocked, and it used Casper's own hands to do it.

chapters.title: What the Desk Remembers
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. Reviewing years of guest ledgers and overheard confidences, Casper maps three deaths ruled accidental — a fisherman, an archivist, a caretaker — all connected to the Voss estate. Police dismiss them; Casper doesn't. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into obsession as Casper realizes the pattern predates their arrival in town.

chapters.title: The Matriarch's Tea
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. Invited to Voss House by Eleanor Voss, the founder's widow and Casper's anonymous benefactor, Casper is charmed, warned, and subtly interrogated. Eleanor mentions the letter with unsettling precision. Emotional beat: warmth laced with dread — Casper owes this woman everything, which makes her a suspect they don't want.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven in Salt
chapters.summary: Detective Imogen Reyes, POV (first shift). Reyes reopens the file and finds every alibi from the night Voss disappeared interlocks too perfectly — four families covering one story for thirty years. She notices Casper asking the same questions. Emotional beat: professional suspicion curdling into reluctant respect between two people circling the same truth.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. In the hotel's long-term storage, Casper finds a hidden ledger proving the founding families ran contraband through the pier — and that Voss planned to confess publicly. The three dead were all holders of copies. Emotional beat: vertigo; the beloved town was built on a crime, and Casper now holds the proof everyone killed for.

chapters.title: A Threat at Room Nine
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. Someone ransacks Casper's room at the hotel; the ledger copy is taken but a decoy remains. A warning note quotes the confession verbatim — meaning the sender knows Casper delivered it. Emotional beat: fear turning personal; the watcher has become the watched, and duty to the truth now costs real safety.

chapters.title: Reyes Draws the Circle
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. Reyes confronts Casper with evidence of their interference and instead of arresting them, proposes partnership: her warrant power, his pattern-reading. Together they narrow the suspects to those still alive from that night — including Eleanor. Emotional beat: trust forged under pressure; love against duty begins its quiet argument.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Alternating Casper/Reyes. An extreme low tide exposes remains beneath the old pier — Voss after all, but with evidence he died protecting someone. The confession letter's true addressee is revealed: not police, but the person Voss loved. Emotional beat: grief reframing the mystery; the founder wasn't silenced, he sacrificed.

chapters.title: The Confession Delivered
chapters.summary: Casper, POV. Climax. Casper confronts Eleanor, who admits she covered the death to save her son and paid for the town's silence ever since — the benefactions, the job, the letter's delivery, all penance aimed at Casper. She offers a final bargain: bury it, and be family forever. Emotional beat: heartbreak at the crossroads of gratitude and integrity.

chapters.title: Belonging, Honestly Kept
chapters.summary: Casper and Reyes, alternating final sections. Eleanor surrenders publicly rather than let her son take the fall; the town reels, then slowly exhales. Casper, no longer invisible, chooses to stay — not as the hotel's ghost, but as the man who told the truth and was kept anyway. Emotional beat: resolution and quiet joy; belonging earned at full price, love chosen over safety.
